MACHINE-RESEARCHED PROPOSAL — Level 2. Confirm, correct or reject at validation.
Egypt has legislated and begun issuing a national digital property ID, but the evidence does not show a formal digital land/plot registration system. Law No. 88 of 2025 mandates a centralised digital database assigning a unique ID to each real estate asset, and Egypt has issued nearly 30 million National Property Identification Numbers. However, the World Bank states that the National Property ID functions solely as a unique digital identifier, not legal registration, and that legal ownership continues to depend exclusively on registration with the Real Estate Registry. Formal registration coverage is below 10%, rollout is expected to take up to five years and is voluntary, and the authority to oversee the data system is still to be determined by Prime Ministerial decree. This makes the current capability an early/ad hoc digital property database rather than an operational registration system.
Why not L3: L3 requires an operational digital land/plot registration system with defined ownership and partial coverage. The documents show the digital property ID is not legal registration or proof of ownership; legal ownership depends on the separate Real Estate Registry. Defined ownership and operational registration are therefore not evidenced, and the World Bank notes fragmented databases and overlapping institutional responsibilities.
